A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same opinion paper, with matching authors, title, and central argument. All pages are readable, including the references. Neither version contains appendices, figures, tables, or displayed equations.

before.justification: v1 synthesizes cited research and offers conceptual arguments and recommendations. It reports no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

after.justification: v2 remains a conceptual opinion paper. Its added examples and empirical observations are attributed to other studies; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

M1.justification: Neither version proposes an algorithm or model with an implemented procedure. The added measurement recommendations and cautions do not introduce or modify a computational method.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets. The new discussions of registers, communication modes, and cross-language differences introduce conceptual considerations without evaluating additional tasks or populations.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates a proposed method against baselines. Newly cited diversity measures and studies remain related work rather than experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an executed experimental protocol. Section 3.3 revises advice about validating measures against datasets with known diversity differences, but does not implement that evaluation.

E4.justification: Neither version contains original ablations, robustness tests, error analyses, or case studies. The added cross-language cautions discuss previously published findings without conducting supplementary analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Their discussion of measurement reliability is conceptual.

E6.justification: Neither version reports results produced by this work. The new observations about lemmatization errors and the relationship between type-token ratio and morphological complexity are explicitly attributed to prior studies.

T1.justification: The operational description of data diversity is retained, and neither version develops formal mathematics or proofs. Added explanations of bias, validity, continuity, and maximality remain conceptual rather than mathematical definitions or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, interdisciplinary thesis, monolingual focus, and six concluding recommendations retain their meaning. Clarifying that the recommendations are language-independent and calling them immediately actionable does not redefine the core contribution.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the conceptual qualifications: Section 1 distinguishes diversity from representativeness and bias; Section 3.1 adds situational factors and missing register metadata; Section 3.2 explains tool availability, lemmatization errors, and morphological confounds across languages. Section 3.3 also reframes validity evidence and elaborates theoretical desiderata. These broaden the interpretation and applicability guidance, although the standalone Limitations discussion is substantively retained.

D1.justification: Neither version supplies implementation settings, computational resources, or access instructions for original code or data. General references to tokenizers, parsers, and embeddings do not disclose a reproducible implementation.

R1.justification: v2 adds an explicit comparison with Estève et al. (2025) and supporting literature on representativeness, registers, cross-language measurement, and psychometrics. These extend the existing interdisciplinary positioning. Publication updates for retained works, including Su et al. and Birhane/Prabhu, do not constitute new research relationships.

P1.justification: v2 adds named discussion paragraphs, rewrites portions of Sections 2 and 3.3, and makes wording, acknowledgment, and bibliographic edits. The section hierarchy, narrative order, and much of the original prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Both versions retain the same text-only, two-column format and typography. Additional prose and references cause pagination changes, without introducing figures, tables, or a substantive layout redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 improves conceptual precision by distinguishing diversity from representativeness and bias, and strengthens practical guidance through specific cross-language measurement cautions and clearer validity examples. These useful refinements build on an argument and six recommendations already present in v1; they support a limited overall quality improvement.
